summary: In major space developments, NASA has awarded SpaceX three additional crew flights to the International Space Station. On the military and defense front, the U.S. Space Force is prototyping new software to fuse commercial and military space tracking data, the Pentagon selected two companies for a reconnaissance satellite demonstration, and France’s 2035 national security plan warns of increased conflict in outer space and at sea. Internationally, Europe’s space tracking program is seeing growing interest and support. In the commercial sector, Space Cargo Unlimited booked one-third of its Starfall capacity, while satellite firm Terran Orbital promoted Margherita Cardi to vice president of European operations and head of strategic programs. Scientific progress includes observations by the joint NASA-JAXA XRISM mission of a pulsar gathering its companion’s wind, NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope spotting an out-of-sync galaxy, and the continued integration of NASA's COSI telescope. Additionally, scientists simulated cosmic crashes to evaluate the habitability of icy moons, while solar system research indicates that the earliest solid bodies formed from high-temperature materials rather than ice. Looking ahead, space observers should watch for Albania to formally sign the Artemis Accords during an upcoming ceremony with NASA.
